questions.text: When someone disappoints or wrongs me, my first instinct is to consider what they might be carrying rather than focus on how I have been affected.
My sense of contentment remains relatively stable across good and difficult seasons, rather than rising and falling with circumstances.
When outcomes are outside my control, I am able to release them without extended anxiety or mental rehearsal.
When people or processes move more slowly than I would like, I respond with steadiness rather than frustration.
I am attentive to the needs of people around me, even when I am preoccupied with my own concerns.
My private behavior and my public behavior are consistent. I live with similar integrity when no one is watching.
I follow through on commitments even when my motivation has faded or circumstances have changed.
I am able to correct, confront, or disagree with someone without leaving them feeling diminished or attacked.
When an appetite -- food, attention, entertainment, anger, lust -- pulls at me, I am generally able to pause before acting.
I find myself keeping a mental ledger of how people have treated me and adjusting what I give them accordingly.
When life feels flat or hard, I struggle to access any genuine sense of gladness.
My mind tends to loop on worst-case scenarios, especially at night or in quiet moments.
I find myself mentally rehearsing a frustrated response before I have even reacted outwardly.
I tend to move past people I encounter in daily life without really noticing them.
There are meaningful gaps between what I profess publicly and how I actually behave in private.
I tend to start commitments strong and let them quietly fade when they become inconvenient.
When I am frustrated, my strength tends to come out as sharpness or force rather than restraint.
My actions are more often driven by what I feel in the moment than by what I have decided is true.
When a relationship requires sacrifice with no clear personal benefit, I tend to lean in rather than pull back.
I find genuine delight in ordinary moments, not just in milestones or achievements.
I bring a calming presence to tense or uncertain situations rather than adding to the friction.
When I am wronged or treated unfairly, I am able to wait and trust rather than retaliate or force resolution.
I find myself looking for practical ways to make things easier for the people in my life.
When I see an opportunity to do what is right, I act on it even when it is inconvenient or costly.
I sustain spiritual rhythms and disciplines through dry seasons, not only when they feel rewarding.
My strength and conviction tend to express themselves with restraint and care rather than force.
I have established rhythms and boundaries in my life that hold even when I do not feel like maintaining them.
